description: We are Cosmic Commit, a team of second-year B.Tech Computer Science students from Kochi, Kerala, India. We are building a browser-based game for the "Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer" challenge, where kids aged 7 to 12 run a lunar outpost and learn that every decision has a cost: power spent on science means less for life support, and stronger shielding means less power tonight. We want to ground the game in real NASA data, such as DONKI space weather.
summary:
Mission Control is an interactive educational space exploration game that challenges students to experience the decisions involved in establishing a sustainable human outpost beyond Earth. Players take on the role of a space scientist, choose between a lunar or Martian mission, manage essential resources such as oxygen, fuel, food, power and crew morale, and respond to unexpected mission challenges.

Through interactive scenarios, exploration activities and decision-based gameplay, players discover how the Moon and Mars differ and why careful planning is essential for astronaut survival. The lunar path focuses on exploring the lunar environment and investigating potential water ice resources, while the Mars path introduces the challenges of exploring the Red Planet and searching for signs of past or present life.

By transforming complex space exploration concepts into an engaging game, Mission Control makes space science more accessible to students and encourages scientific curiosity, critical thinking and responsible decision-making.
details:
How Mission Control Works

Mission Control is designed as a decision-based educational simulation that takes players through the different stages of a space exploration mission.

Players begin at Mission Control, where they prepare for launch, select equipment and choose their destination: the Moon or Mars.

The game then takes them through a shared space journey, where they encounter unexpected situations and must make decisions that influence their mission resources.

Two Exploration Paths

Moon Mission: Players explore the lunar environment, learn about its extreme conditions, investigate the lunar south pole and discover why water ice is important for future exploration.

Mars Mission: Players explore the Red Planet, learn about its thin atmosphere, cold environment and dust storms, and investigate evidence of ancient water and the scientific search for signs of past life.

Resource Management and Decision-Making

Throughout the mission, players manage five essential resources:

  • Fuel
  • Oxygen
  • Food
  • Power
  • Crew morale

Their choices affect resource availability, mission progress and the final outcome. Interactive challenges and educational facts help players understand the scientific reasoning behind each decision.

Technology Used

The project was developed using React.js, JavaScript, HTML and CSS, with Vite as the development and build tool. GitHub was used for version control and collaboration, and Vercel was used for deployment.

Benefits and Intended Impact

Mission Control turns space exploration concepts into an interactive learning experience. It encourages students to think critically, understand planetary environments, explore scientific challenges and appreciate the importance of sustainable resource management in future human space missions.

Its creative approach combines game-based learning, planetary exploration and decision-making to make space science more accessible and engaging for young learners.
